recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Any future removal or externalization of Encounter.dietPreference should proceed under a dedicated PA/PC issue, not by reopening FHIR-4003.
issue_request: FHIR-4003 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification DSTU1 PA issue asking whether Encounter.hospitalization.diet should map to NutritionOrder/NutritionRequest because the old coded diet entry did not appear aligned with a full nutrition order. The final disposition renamed the field to dietPreference, kept it as a coded preference, and asked for clearer hospitalization/admission descriptive text.
initial_application: Commit 8fb7336ca520b2fabc07796058cd9c9aa4ea19f3 renamed Encounter.hospitalization.diet to Encounter.hospitalization.dietPreference, changed the label to diet preferences reported by the patient, and added requirements text saying complete nutrition needs should use the nutritionOrder resource that links to Encounter. Commit 4c1752027ccab99fa86adf2f48825e92aca7101a updated the hospitalization short/comment to describe admission to a healthcare service and broader admission contexts.
additional_context: Encounter and NutritionOrder are active current-build resources. Later FHIR-32390 renamed Encounter.hospitalization to Encounter.admission and preserved migration mappings, while FHIR-14157 moved dietPreference to top-level Encounter and deferred the separate dietPreference-to-extension/removal question for PA/PC follow-up. The combined branch already contains a FHIR-14157 human-review audit for that deferred question.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. Current source already carries the FHIR-4003 decision: Encounter.dietPreference remains a coded preference, its requirements text points complete nutrition needs to NutritionOrder linked to Encounter, NutritionOrder.encounter references Encounter, and Encounter.admission describes the broad admission scope.
